answers.q1: Cargo (Rust workspace, edition 2024, MSRV 1.96). Cargo has no separate install step, because dependencies are fetched on build. Run `cargo build` from the repo root, or `cargo fetch` to only download dependencies. CI builds with `cargo build --verbose --workspace`.
answers.q2: `cargo test --all`. This is the documented command in AGENTS.md. CI instead runs `cargo test --verbose --workspace --features unstable-index` and `cargo test --verbose --workspace --features pcre2`.
answers.q3: `cargo test --test integration regression::`. tests/regression.rs is a module of the single `integration` test target (tests/tests.rs, `autotests = false`), so it can't be run as `--test regression`. The `regression::` filter selects its tests.
answers.q4: The CI formatting check is `cargo fmt --all --check` (rustfmt.toml sets max_width 79). The CI docs check is `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace`. CI has no clippy step. It also runs `ci/test-complete`, which checks zsh completions against `--help` and needs a built `rg` and zsh.
answers.q5: I found no vendored directories. Lockfiles are tool-generated, so don't hand-edit `Cargo.lock` or `fuzz/Cargo.lock`. `HomebrewFormula` is a symlink to `pkg/brew`, so edit the files under `pkg/brew` rather than the link. The build script (build.rs) generates shell completions and man pages into `target/`, and those must not be edited. They come from the flag docs in `crates/core/flags/defs.rs`, so change that file instead. `crates/core/flags/complete/zsh.rs` matched my search for generated-file markers, but I didn't open it to confirm it is generated. `ci/sha256-releases` is probably release-generated, but I didn't check it either.

q1.reason: Names Cargo, says no separate install step, and gives `cargo build` / `cargo fetch`, matching ACCEPT.

q2.reason: Gives `cargo test --all`, which is an accepted command; the CI details are harmless extras.

q3.reason: `cargo test --test integration regression::` matches an ACCEPT form and correctly explains why `--test regression` fails.

q4.reason: Gives `cargo fmt --all --check` and the cargo doc check, and correctly states CI has no clippy step.

q5.reason: Correctly names Cargo.lock and target/ and finds no vendored directories, but also claims generated files that are not hand-editable (fuzz/Cargo.lock, pkg/brew handling, flags/defs.rs guidance) and hedges on unverified files like zsh.rs and ci/sha256-releases, which blurs the 'none' truth.
